edits.match: Most people who follow their rehabilitation programme resume nearly all normal activities within about three to six weeks, and daily life improves for the great majority.
edits.replacement: Daily life improves for the great majority.
edits.reason: WRONG: 'nearly all normal activities within three to six weeks' is not in the NHS source and conflicts with the record's own (pre-patch) timeline of walking without aids at about six weeks and driving at 6-8 weeks.

notes: NHS excerpts support: blood clots (seek urgent help for chest pain/breathlessness), wound and joint infection possibly needing further surgery, vessel/nerve/ligament damage, numbness of skin usually permanent, persistent stiffness or pain, instability needing further surgery, risk higher with age/health/obesity, swelling common, warning signs of redness/fever/pus, implant lasting ~25 years on average. Deep infection 1% and 2-6 weeks of anticoagulant prophylaxis predate the patch. No protected field (medications) changed.
